newsitem.title: RUSSIA: TengizChevroil says oil output to rise this year.
newsitem.headline: TengizChevroil says oil output to rise this year.

text.p: Chevron Corp and Mobil Corp's TengizChevroil venture expects to boost production capacity to 170,000-180,000 barrels per day later this year, TCO general director Nick Zana said on Tuesday.
Zana, speaking after an energy conference, said that output last month at the giant Tengiz field in Kazakhstan was 600,000 tonnes, or around 144,000 barrels per day.
He also said TCO would spend $1.6 billion over the next three years in operating and capital expenditures on Tengiz, the world's largest discovered oil field in the last 20 years.

Debottlenecking procedures planned later this year at the production site, in western Kazakhstan, would temporarily bring output down before boosting it. TCO plans to spend $350 million to carry out the procedures to raise production capacity.
Peak output is targeted at 30-35 million tonnes a year (600,000-700,000 bpd) by 2010.
TCO output has sometimes fluctuated on various factors, mostly limited access to oil export pipelines, but has been rising steadily overall. Output at one point in January was 160,000 bpd.
Chevron owns 10 percent of TCO, and Mobil and the Kazakh government each own 25 percent. Chevron has a deal to sell Russian oil company LUKoil a total five percent stake in the venture.
Tengiz has estimated oil reserves of at least 6-9 billion barrels as well as 1.8 trillion cubic metres of associated gas.
